body:
Found by review of getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#262 (switching an own-repo instance back to `wave_mode = "stack"`, template v0.58.0). Related: #463, #591, #185.

## Two defects

**1. Middle-wave PRs break within the same run.** `integrate.fold` rebuilds `pdca-integration/<base>` from the base on every fold, re-applying each accepted `patch.diff` as a new `pdca-integrate:*` commit, and force-pushes it. A wave-1 PR is opened against that branch (own repo); after wave 1 is accepted, the next fold rebuilds the same branch with waves 0..1 as NEW commits. The wave-1 PR's base now contains its own change (as a different commit), so the PR goes empty, conflicting or DCO-red before any human can merge it. Any batch with three or more waves hits this inside one invocation.

**2. Wave 1+ PRs never reach the target.** For an own-repo target, `publish.py` sets a wave>0 PR's `--base` to the integration branch. Nothing retargets those PRs and nothing opens an integration → target PR, so merging them bottom-up merges into the integration branch only; only wave 0 lands on the target.

## Fix (implemented as an instance delta downstream)

- **Fold append-only over the real PR branches.** Continue the integration branch from its current tip (start at the base only the first time), `git merge --no-ff --signoff` each accepted bundle's PUBLISHED branch (`publish.json`'s `branch`) that is not already an ancestor, and push without force. No base an open PR sits on is ever rewritten; the stacked branches inherit the predecessors' own commits (same SHAs).
- **Every wave PR targets the real base.** A wave>0 bundle's branch is still cut from the integration branch (it builds and verifies on its predecessors), but its PR's `--base` is the target. Merging bottom-up lands everything; because the predecessors' commits are the same SHAs, the dependent's diff shrinks to its own change as soon as they merge. A hand-declared `Stacks on:` parent (#123) keeps its PR-branch base (GitHub retargets it on merge).
- Merge commits carry `--signoff`: a DCO check that reads every PR commit sees them.

Cost: until its predecessors merge, a dependent PR's diff shows their changes too.
title: stack mode: a multi-wave own-repo run breaks its own middle-wave PRs, and wave 1+ PRs never reach the target
